# API reference customisation

A Python extension gives you two ways to customise your API reference.

- Use a [hook](#hooks) to run a function when Great Docs handles an event. For
  example, you can leave an object out of the reference or edit its docstring.
- Use a [custom renderer](#custom-renderers) to change how objects or pages
  appear. For example, you can hide class signatures or add a note below each
  object's docstring.

## Extension setup

Set `api_reference_extension` to the path to your Python file, relative to
`great-docs.yml`. In this example, the two files sit side by side.

```{.yaml filename="docs/great-docs.yml"}
api_reference_extension: _api_reference_extension.py
```

You can also use an absolute path to the `.py` file. Leave
`api_reference_extension` at its default of `null` to use the built-in output.

Define a `setup(extension)` function in the Python file to register your hooks
and/or select custom renderers.

## Hooks {#hooks}

Each decorator registers a function for one event. Both events let you change
the reference pages and `llms-full.txt`.

| Event | Decorator | What your function returns |
|---|---|---|
| Great Docs finds the object to document | `@extension.on_object_resolved` | The object, with any docstring edits, or `None` to exclude it |
| Great Docs finishes parsing a docstring | `@extension.on_docstring_parsed` | The sections to keep, in the order you want them to appear |

### A note in the text export

To include a note in both the reference page and `llms-full.txt`, add it to the
docstring itself. For example, point `api_reference_extension` at the following
file and rebuild.

```{.python filename="docs/_add_note_extension.py"}
import griffe as gf

from great_docs.extensions import Extension


def setup(extension: Extension) -> None:
    @extension.on_object_resolved
    def add_note(obj: gf.Object | gf.Alias) -> gf.Object | gf.Alias:
        if obj.docstring is not None:
            obj.docstring.value += "\n\nThis description includes a project note."
        return obj
```

If an object has aliases, editing its docstring changes the text under every
name. Excluding the object also excludes its aliases.

## Custom renderers {#custom-renderers}

A renderer controls how Great Docs displays an object or page. To exclude class
signatures, subclass `ClassRenderer` and pass your subclass to `Renderers` in
`setup`.

```{.python filename="docs/_signature_extension.py"}
from great_docs.extensions import Extension
from great_docs.pandoc.blocks import BlockContent
from great_docs.rendering import ClassRenderer, Renderers


class QuietClass(ClassRenderer):
    def render_signature(self) -> BlockContent:
        return None


def setup(extension: Extension) -> None:
    extension.set_renderers(Renderers(classes=QuietClass))
```

The source link still appears if one is available. Great Docs omits the Usage
row when there is neither a signature nor a source link.

You can register a hook and a custom renderer in the same `setup` function.
For example, add the `set_renderers` call above to the `setup` function that
registers `add_note` to include the note and hide class signatures.

To change the label that readers see for each function in a summary, override
`summary_name` on `FunctionRenderer`.

```{.python filename="docs/_summary_extension.py"}
from great_docs.extensions import Extension
from great_docs.rendering import FunctionRenderer, Renderers


class LabelledFunction(FunctionRenderer):
    @property
    def summary_name(self) -> str:
        return f"Run {super().summary_name}"


def setup(extension: Extension) -> None:
    extension.set_renderers(Renderers(functions=LabelledFunction))
```

You can supply a renderer for `classes`, `functions`, `attributes`,
`type_aliases`, `modules`, `api_pages`, `reference_index` or
`reference_sections`. Each takes a subclass of the corresponding renderer.
Great Docs uses its defaults for any you leave out. The subclasses apply only to
this project's API reference.

| To change                                             | Override                                  |
|-------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------|
| An object's label, in its heading and page title      | `render_title_content`                    |
| The heading around that label, or whether it appears  | `render_title`                            |
| The description or signature                          | `render_description`, `render_signature`  |
| Docstring sections and their headings                 | `render_docstring_body`                   |
| Summaries of members, whether on this page or another | `render_members_summary(kind, renderers)` |
| Documentation for members on this page                | `render_members_body(kind, renderers)`    |
| The whole body, including member groups               | `render_body`                             |
| Summary entries or their labels                       | `render_summary`, `summary_name`          |

Return `None` from a method that renders a block to exclude that part of the page.
To exclude summary entries, return an empty sequence from `render_summary()`.
Hidden members still belong to the reference and appear in its inventories.

### Shared formatting with `object_renderer_mixin`

To add a note to every object's documentation, write a mixin that overrides
`render_docstring_body` and pass it to `Renderers` as `object_renderer_mixin`.
Call `super().render_docstring_body()` to keep the usual docstring sections
and append the note after them.

```{.python filename="docs/_api_reference_extension.py"}
from great_docs.extensions import Extension
from great_docs.pandoc.blocks import BlockContent, Blocks, Para
from great_docs.rendering import Renderers


class AppendNoteMixin:
    def render_docstring_body(self) -> BlockContent:
        body = super().render_docstring_body()
        return Blocks([body, Para("Prepared for this project's documentation.")])


def setup(extension: Extension) -> None:
    extension.set_renderers(Renderers(object_renderer_mixin=AppendNoteMixin))
```

On a class page, the note appears before the member groups. Each method
documented on the same page gets its own note, even if its docstring body is
empty.

The mixin applies to the default renderers for classes, functions, attributes,
type aliases and modules. To use the same formatting in a custom object
renderer, inherit from the mixin first. For example, declare
`class LabelledFunction(AppendNoteMixin, FunctionRenderer)`.

#### Page details {#page-details}

Check `self.context.authored_name` to limit the note to a single name.
For example, add these lines after the call to `super()` to show the note
only on the object documented as `Document`.

```python
if self.context.authored_name != "Document":
    return body
```

To select by page instead, check `self.context.page_path`, the QMD path
relative to the output directory. Methods shown on a class page share that
page's path.

### Examples in docstrings {#example-in-docstrings}

Suppose a docstring's Usage section shows `old_usage()` and you want the page
to show `new_usage()`. Override `render_docstring_body` to replace the text in
the rendered docstring sections, including fenced code examples.

```{.python filename="docs/_usage_extension.py"}
from great_docs.extensions import Extension
from great_docs.pandoc.blocks import BlockContent
from great_docs.rendering import Renderers


class ReplaceUsageMixin:
    def render_docstring_body(self) -> BlockContent:
        body = super().render_docstring_body()
        if body is None:
            return None
        return str(body).replace("old_usage()", "new_usage()")


def setup(extension: Extension) -> None:
    extension.set_renderers(Renderers(object_renderer_mixin=ReplaceUsageMixin))
```

The opening line of the docstring appears in the object's description. Use
`render_description` to change it, `render_title` to change the heading, or
`render_usage_source` to change the automatic Usage label and source link.

## Preview and freeze {#preview-and-freeze}

If your extension reads files, tell Great Docs which ones to watch in `setup`.
You can name a file, use a pattern or watch a whole directory.

```python
extension.watch("data.txt")
extension.watch("data/*.txt")
extension.watch("examples")
```

Use absolute paths or paths relative to the extension file. If preview asks
you to restart after you add a file to watch, rerun `great-docs build --watch`.

With `freeze: auto`, changes to the extension or its watched files cause
affected code to run again. With `freeze: true`, refresh the saved results
yourself.

To refresh a page explicitly, build the project once, then pass the generated
page's path to `great-docs freeze`. For example, the following command runs the
current customised page and saves its results.

```bash
great-docs freeze docs/_quarto/default/reference/Document.qmd
```

Use the path for your own layout and reference entry. For more on refreshing
pages, see [Freeze](freeze.qmd). For help choosing which objects to document
and where they appear, see [API documentation](api-documentation.qmd).
